nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Account Settings (scroll 1)
caption: Account Settings tab — top section. Left: core account fields — Account ID, Email ID, Account Currency, Subscription Plan (e.g. free_trial), Account Product Type (CX for new clients on Plivo CX console; API for older clients with legacy console access), Enabled (Yes/No — if No, all services fail), Voice Enabled, Zentrunk Enabled, Zentrunk Jitter Enabled, User Active, Staff User, Proof Verified, Credits. Right-side action buttons (scroll 1): Enable Account / Disable User — enable or disable the account; Disable Messages at Operator Level — not used by support (seniors have never used it); Manage Cards / Manage Bank Accounts — card and banking management; Set CPS — change outbound calls-per-second limit; Set Inbound CPS — change inbound CPS limit; Set Zentrunk Outbound CPS — Zentrunk-specific CPS; Disable SMS / Disable MMS / Disable WhatsApp — disable respective messaging channels; Set SMS MPS — set SMS messages-per-second rate limit. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search by email/Auth ID] → Account Settings.

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Account Settings (scroll 2)
caption: Account Settings tab — middle section. Left: Auth ID (API key identifier used in all API calls), CPS Allowed, Inbound CPS Allowed, Zentrunk CPS Allowed, Zentrunk Account ID, SMS MPS Allowed, Zentrunk Routing Profile, Stir Attestation Config, Zentrunk Voice Routing Profile, Zentrunk Media PCAP Capture, Account Type (Standard), Credit Limit, Billing Type (Prepaid/Postpaid), Product Plan (e.g. standard_nv), Risk Rating, Customer Type (e.g. Regular Customer), SMS Carrier Profile. Right-side action buttons (scroll 2): Set MMS MPS; Set as Staff User — not used by support; Change Email — update login email; Edit Product Plan — support does this in collaboration with the product ops team; most clients are on standard plan but some are on non-standard plans; Update Account Product Type — support does this: CX = new clients on the Plivo CX console, API = older clients who have access to both legacy and new consoles; Update Subscription Plan — support can change upon customer request; Verify Proof — card verification: enter Auth ID, click button, enter ticket ID and comment, card gets verified; used when card verification gets stuck; Edit Zentrunk Routing Profile / Update Bulk Routing Profile / Edit Stir Attestation Config / Edit SMS Carrier Profile Group; Update Risk Status / Mark as Risky — flag or update risk classification; Refund — issue credit refund; Reset Login Attempts / Reset Email 2FA Attempts — unlock locked accounts; Disable Zentrunk. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → Account Settings (scroll down).

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Account Settings (scroll 3)
caption: Account Settings tab — lower-middle section. Left: SMS Carrier Profile Group, SMS Routing Strategy, SMS Cost Check, Voice Carrier Type (Global Plivo Carrier or custom), Plivo Carrier Fallback (No = single carrier, higher failure risk), Bulk Call Enabled, Auto Payment Approval, Show Billing Data, Last Login, Phone Verification Attempts, Card Verification Needed, Account Notes (always check — internal investigation notes added by support). Right-side action buttons (scroll 3): Disable Zentrunk Jitter; Enable Zentrunk Media PCAP Capture — turn on PCAP before asking customer to reproduce a failing call for analysis; Enable Bulk Call — not used by support; Disable Voice — disable voice product for account; Manage USD Bank Transfer — not used by support; Download CDR / Download MDR — download call/message detail records; Add Account Notes — add internal investigation notes (always use to log ticket ID and findings); Change Voice Carrier Type — switch between Global Plivo Carrier and custom routing; Change Customer Type — not used by support; Update Profile Information; Schedule Conversion to Postpaid — converts account from prepaid to postpaid billing; form fields: Credit Limit, Re-enter Credit Limit, Payment Period in days (default 30), Convert now OR End of month option, Comments; Enable Fallback for Plivo Voice Carriers — enable carrier fallback when primary carrier is failing; Enable SMS Cost Check — not used by support; Disable Auto Payment Approval; Disable Showing Billing Data. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → Account Settings (scroll further).

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Account Settings (scroll 4)
caption: Account Settings tab — bottom section. Left: Auto Recharge (Disabled/Enabled), Auto Recharge Threshold, Sandbox Numbers, Payment Period, Risk Status (e.g. low_risk), 2-FA verified number, Internal Outbound/Inbound Delivery Rate Alerts, Content View Authorization, 10DLC Brand Cap, Is Campaign Paused, MMS MPS Allowed, MMS Daily Max Upload Limit, SMS Disabled, MMS Enabled, WhatsApp Enabled. Right-side action buttons (scroll 4): Update Invoice Data — updates invoice fields (Key, Value, Comment); not used by support; Disable 2 Factor Authentication; Update Tax Exemption; Enable SubAccount Billing; Set MMS Media Upload Limit; Switch to USD Billing; Set Brand Cap — set 10DLC brand cap limit; Pause 10DLC Campaign Registration; Set Outbound Delivery Rate Alert / Set Inbound Delivery Rate Alert — configure SMS delivery rate alerts; Edit Recharge Limit; Check Email Bounce Status — not used by support; Pause Overall Scoped Alerts; Enable SSO; Port-out no response config — not used by support; config options: OFF or NO (determines auto-response behaviour when port-out request receives no response). Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → Account Settings (scroll to bottom).

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Customer Profile
caption: Customer Profile tab in Ryuk for a customer account. Shows customer identity and registration details: Username (hashed internal ID), Full Name, Email ID, Account Time Zone, Country, Company name, Registered IP address, Registered Region (AWS region e.g. ap-south-1), Joined Date, Authenticated Phone Number, Phone Number Country, Verification Code, Billing Email. Used to verify the customer's business identity, check their country/region for compliance purposes, and confirm billing contact details. Different from Account Settings — this is the customer-facing profile, not the technical account config. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search by email/Auth ID] → Customer Profile tab.

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Sub Account Details
caption: Sub Account Details tab in Ryuk. Shows sub-accounts (child accounts) linked to the parent account. Search by Auth ID with a status dropdown filter. If no sub-accounts exist, shows 'No subaccounts found for this account'. Used to check whether a customer has sub-accounts — relevant when a ticket is raised by a sub-account and you need to find the parent, or when sub-account permissions are the root cause of an issue. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search] → Sub Account Details tab.

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Additional Feature (scroll 1)
caption: Additional Feature tab in Ryuk — first scroll. Shows per-account feature flags beyond standard Voice/SMS. Table columns: Feature (human-readable name and internal flag key), Status (green checkmark = enabled, red X = disabled), Feature Type (Temp Feature, Inherited Feature, Permanent Feature — indicates source/permanence), Sub Account toggle, Action toggle (enable/disable). Feature flags visible in scroll 1: SMS Destination Number Validation (dlt_number_validation) — validates DLT template for Indian numbers; SMS Landline Texting Flag (landline_texting); sms_disabled; auto_replace_enabled; ip_auth — IP-based authentication; Premium Numbers Block (premium_numbers_block) — blocks premium rate numbers; Call Insights premium user (callinsights_ntp_enabled); Non-Verified DID Allowed (non_verified_did_allowed) — allows unverified DIDs; Block unregistered 10dlc traffic — SMS (tendlc_block_unregistered_traffic); Voice Destination Number Validation (voice_dest_val); Block Verify (verify_disabled). Use this tab to check or toggle special feature behaviour for an account — especially DLT validation, IP auth, and 10DLC blocking flags. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search] → Additional Feature tab.

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Additional Feature (scroll 2)
caption: Additional Feature tab in Ryuk — second scroll, showing additional feature flags lower in the list. Features visible: Enable Port In (port_in) — allows number porting into Plivo; good_account flag; Call Insights (callstats); Call Queue (call_queue); Strip URL Scheme From Message Content (sms_transform_urls_in_content) — strips http/https from URLs in SMS; Voice Fraud Analysis (voice_monitoring_enabled) — enables fraud monitoring on voice calls. Use this tab in combination with scroll 1 to see the full set of feature flags enabled for an account. Toggle actions are available per feature. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search] → Additional Feature tab (scroll down).

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → WhatsApp Accounts
caption: WhatsApp Accounts tab in Ryuk. Shows WhatsApp Business API (WABA) accounts linked to the customer. When no WhatsApp accounts are configured, shows 'No WABA's are present for this account'. Used to check if a customer has WhatsApp Business API set up through Plivo, and to look up their WABA configuration details when troubleshooting WhatsApp delivery issues. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search] → WhatsApp Accounts tab.

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → SMPP Accounts
caption: SMPP Accounts tab in Ryuk. Shows SMPP (Short Message Peer-to-Peer) connections configured for the account. Search by Auth ID with status dropdown. Add New button creates a new SMPP connection. When no SMPP accounts exist, shows 'Sorry! No SMPP Records found!'. Used to verify whether a customer has SMPP configured — relevant when troubleshooting SMPP binding failures, credential issues, or delivery problems on the SMPP channel. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search] → SMPP Accounts tab.

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → SMPP Accounts → Add New
caption: Add SMPP Account modal in Ryuk. Used to create a new SMPP connection for a customer account. Fields: Account (Auth ID — pre-filled), SMPP Binds (number of concurrent binds allowed, range 1–6), Username (SMPP login), Password (SMPP password — masked), Enable toggle. Click Create to save. The SMPP credentials generated here are what the customer uses to connect their SMPP client to Plivo's SMPP gateway. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → SMPP Accounts tab → Add New button.

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Carrier Relations Accounts
caption: Carrier Relations Accounts tab in Ryuk. Shows carrier relationship configuration for the account — relevant for BYOC (Bring Your Own Carrier) customers. Fields displayed: Account ID (internal carrier relations ID), Email ID, Enabled (Yes/No), User Active, SMS Carrier Profile Group (e.g. Standard), SMS Routing Strategy (e.g. Manual), Voice Carrier Type (e.g. Global Plivo Carrier), Plivo Carrier Fallback (No = no fallback), Bulk Call Enabled (No). Use this tab when investigating carrier-specific routing issues, to confirm what SMS carrier profile and routing strategy is assigned, and to check whether fallback is configured. Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search] → Carrier Relations Accounts tab.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline
caption: Voice Call Timeline search page in Ryuk. This is the main voice debugging hub. Has three tabs: Fetch CDRs (search call detail records), Voice Debugger (real-time debugging), Historical CDR Export (bulk CDR export). Enter a call UUID in the search box or use filters to pull up call details. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline.

nav_path: Voice → Recording Storage Management
caption: Recording Storage Management page in Ryuk. Used to manage voice call recordings stored by Plivo for the account. Can view, search, and manage recorded calls. Navigate: Voice → Recording Storage Management.

nav_path: Voice → PCAP Analyser v2
caption: PCAP Analyser v2 in Ryuk. Enter a call UUID to retrieve the PCAP (packet capture) file for that call. Used to analyse SIP signalling and RTP media at the packet level for deep audio quality troubleshooting. Navigate: Voice → PCAP Analyser v2 → enter UUID → fetch PCAP.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs
caption: Fetch CDRs page under Voice → Call Timeline in Ryuk. Search form includes: date range, from/to number, Account Auth ID, hangup cause, direction (inbound/outbound), call status. Results table shows CDRs with columns: date, from, to, direction, duration, hangup cause, status. Click a CDR row to see full CDR detail. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs tab → enter filters → Search.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail
caption: CDR Detail page in Ryuk (top section). Shows complete call details: Account Auth ID, Call UUID (unique identifier for the call), call direction (inbound/outbound), initiation time, answer time, end time, SIP Call Hangup cause, Call Status, Hangup cause code, From number, To number, carrier info. Also has Server Logs tab to see internal system logs. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs → click a CDR row.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail
caption: CDR Detail page scrolled down showing additional call detail fields and the beginning of Server Logs section. Contains billing duration, rate, and other technical fields.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail → Server Logs
caption: Server Logs section within CDR Detail in Ryuk. Shows tabs for different internal system logs: PlivoCloud (application server logs), Outproxy (outbound SIP proxy logs), CDR Worker, MediaServer (media server/RTP logs), SIP Server. Used to trace exactly where a call failed by reading log entries from each component. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs → click CDR → Server Logs section.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail → Server Logs → MediaServer
caption: MediaServer logs tab in CDR Detail Server Logs. Shows RTP media server log entries for the call. Used to diagnose audio quality issues (one-way audio, no audio, echo) by examining what the media server processed. Navigate: Voice → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail → Server Logs → MediaServer tab.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail → Server Logs → MediaServer
caption: MediaServer logs tab (continued scroll) in CDR Detail. More RTP media server log entries for diagnosing audio issues.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail → Customer Debug Logs
caption: Customer Debug Logs tab within CDR Detail in Ryuk. Shows application-level debug logs from the customer's application server (callbacks, XML responses, errors). Used to see what the customer's IVR/application returned and identify XML errors or callback failures. Navigate: Voice → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail → Customer Debug Logs tab.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Timeline v2
caption: CDR Insights page in Ryuk, Call Timeline v2 tab. Accessed by clicking a call UUID in Call Timeline results. Shows a visual timeline of the call with three sub-tabs: Call Progression (detailed event log), Call Timeline (visual), Call Relations (related calls). Top section shows: Call UUID, account Auth ID, from/to numbers, call direction, start/end time, duration, hangup cause. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline → search → click a call UUID → CDR Insights.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Relations & Stats
caption: CDR Insights page showing Call Relations section (related calls linked to same session/conference) and Call Stats section (summary statistics). Used to find parent/child calls and see aggregate call metrics. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline → click UUID → CDR Insights.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Audio Metrics
caption: CDR Insights audio quality metrics in Ryuk. Shows: Jitter (ms), Packet Loss (%), MOS score (Mean Opinion Score, 1-5 scale where 4+ is good, 3.5 is acceptable, below 3 is poor quality). MOS score is the single most important audio quality indicator. Also shows Call Timeline visual with audio quality overlaid. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline → click UUID → CDR Insights → scroll to audio section.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression
caption: Call Progression tab in CDR Insights showing a colour-coded visual timeline of the call. Each segment of the timeline bar represents a different call state/event (ringing, connected, on hold, etc.) with colour coding. Helps visualise where time was spent in a call. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline → click UUID → CDR Insights → Call Progression tab.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Logs
caption: Call Progression Logs table in Ryuk. Shows a chronological event log for the call with columns: Time, Event Type (Xml Event / Callback Event / Call State Event), Event name (Startapp, Speak, Redirect, GetDigits, Record, Dial, Hangup, etc.), Status (200 OK, 408, errors), Issues (warnings like High Latency). Each row can be expanded to see the full payload. This is the primary tool for debugging IVR call flow issues. Navigate: Voice → Call Timeline → click UUID → CDR Insights → Call Progression tab → Logs section.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Logs → Startapp event
caption: Startapp callback event expanded in Call Progression Logs. Shows the POST request payload sent to the customer's application URL when a call starts. Contains: callUUID, from, to, callStatus, direction, and all call parameters. Used to verify the initial webhook was sent and what data the customer's app received. Click the expand arrow on a Startapp row in the logs table.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Logs → Speak XML event
caption: Speak XML event expanded in Call Progression Logs. Shows the XML response from the customer's application containing a <Speak> verb (text-to-speech). Visible fields include the text being spoken, voice, language. Used to verify what TTS was played to the caller. Expand the Speak row in the logs.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Logs → Redirect XML event
caption: Redirect XML event expanded in Call Progression Logs. Shows a <Redirect> verb in the customer's XML response, which transfers call control to a new URL. Contains the redirect URL. Used to trace call flow redirections between different application endpoints.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Logs → Redirect 408 error
caption: Redirect Callback Event showing a 408 Request Timeout error in Call Progression Logs. The Issues column shows a 408 status indicating the customer's callback URL did not respond in time. This causes call failures when the application server is slow or unreachable. Used to identify timeout issues in customer's IVR.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Logs → XML Validation Error
caption: XML Validation Error and Call Hangup events in Call Progression Logs. Shows when Plivo rejected the customer's XML response due to invalid XML syntax or unsupported verbs. The call then hangs up. Used to diagnose XML parsing errors in IVR applications.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Logs → Hangup callback
caption: Final Hangup Callback event expanded in Call Progression Logs. Shows the POST payload sent to the customer's hangup URL, containing: callUUID, callStatus (completed/failed/busy/no-answer), hangupCause, duration, billingDuration, from, to, direction, and all final call parameters. This is the last event in any call and contains the definitive hangup reason.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression
caption: Call Progression timeline for a second example call in Ryuk. Shows the visual timeline bar with events including Startapp, Getdigits (DTMF collection), Call Answered, Redirect, Record, Dial (outbound leg), Call Hangup with WARNING High Latency, Recordstop. This is a typical IVR call flow with recording and dial-out.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Logs
caption: Logs table for second example call showing events: Startapp, Getdigits (DTMF collection), Call Answered, Redirect, Record (call recording started), Dial, Call Hangup, Hangup with WARNING High Latency indicator, Recordstop. High Latency warning appears in the Issues column when callback response time exceeded threshold.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Startapp payload
caption: Startapp POST payload expanded (scroll 1). Shows full webhook parameters including: from, to, callUUID, direction, callStatus, ANI, DNIS, SIP headers, authentication token, session ID. The token field is used for secure callback validation.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Startapp payload
caption: Startapp POST payload (scroll 2). Additional parameters including billing details, account information, and full token/authentication data sent in the startapp callback.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Startapp payload
caption: Startapp POST payload (scroll 3). Final parameters in the startapp callback payload.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → GetDigits XML event
caption: GetDigits XML event expanded in Call Progression Logs (scroll 1). Shows the <GetDigits> verb XML with parameters: finishOnKey (#, *, etc.), validDigits (accepted DTMF tones), timeout (seconds to wait), numDigits (max digits to collect). GetDigits is used to collect DTMF input from callers in IVR menus.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → GetDigits XML event
caption: GetDigits XML event (scroll 2). Additional GetDigits parameters including the action URL where digits will be posted, method, and nested Speak element inside GetDigits for prompting the caller.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Redirect with Record response
caption: Redirect Callback Event showing a 200 OK response containing a Record XML verb. The customer's application responded to a redirect with instructions to start recording the call. Shows the Record URL, callback URL, and recording parameters.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Record XML event
caption: Record XML event expanded in Call Progression Logs. Shows the <Record> verb with parameters: finishOnKey, recordChannelType (stereo/mono), startOnDialAnswer, redirect, timeout, recordSession, method (POST), callbackMethod, transcriptionMethod, playBeep. Used to verify recording configuration.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Dial XML event
caption: Dial XML event expanded in Call Progression Logs. Shows the <Dial> verb parameters: redirect, callerId, callerName, method (POST), callbackMethod, transcriptionMethod. The Dial verb is used to bridge an inbound call to an outbound leg (e.g. agent phone). Used to diagnose why outbound legs are failing.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Dial callback
caption: Dial Callback Event showing the application's response to a dial callback. Contains SIP headers, X-Channel, X-Duration, X-CallType. The callback was to a sales agent action URL. Shows the application acknowledged the dial event and provided redirect instructions.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Hangup High Latency
caption: Hangup Callback Event with WARNING: High Latency in Call Progression Logs. The Issues column shows WARNING High Latency — this means the customer's hangup callback URL responded slowly (high latency). Shows full hangup payload including: callStatus, hangupCause (NORMAL_CLEARING), dialBLegStatus, dialBLegDuration, billingDuration, totalCost. High Latency warning is triggered when callback response exceeds ~3 seconds.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → Hangup High Latency
caption: Hangup Callback Event WARNING High Latency (scroll 2). Continued payload showing full hangup response including latency value (14568ms in example), billingDuration, callStatus. Latency of 14 seconds indicates very slow customer application response.

nav_path: Voice → Call Timeline → CDR Insights → Call Progression → RecordStop callback
caption: RecordStop Callback Event in Call Progression Logs. Sent to the customer's callback URL when a recording is stopped. Contains: recordingURL (where the recording file can be downloaded), recordingDuration (seconds), callerName, callerNumber, recordingStartMs, recordingEndMs, callUUID. Used to verify recording was captured and get the recording URL.

nav_path: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → Country Permissions
caption: Voice Geo Permissions page in Ryuk (Country Permissions tab). Search by Username to see and modify which countries an account can make outbound calls to. Table shows: Country, Continent, Source Of Update (console/admin), Can Override From Console toggle, Custom Block checkbox. Enabled = outbound calls allowed to that country. This is the page to enable or block specific countries for voice calls. Navigate: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → enter username → Country Permissions tab.

nav_path: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → Country Permissions (scroll 2)
caption: Voice Geo Permissions — Country Permissions tab, scroll 2. Search by username and select account. Table columns: Country, Continent, Source of Update, Can Override From Console (customer-visible toggle in Plivo console — allows customer to self-enable/disable), Custom Block (support-set block per account). Countries visible: Canada (North America — Can Override=ON, Custom Block=checked), Cocos (Keeling) Islands (Asia — OFF), Democratic Republic of the Congo (Africa — OFF), Central African Republic (Africa — OFF). Bulk actions bar: Select All Countries, Deselect All Countries, Hard Disable (platform-level block, cannot be overridden), Revert Hard Disable, Cancel, Save Changes. Use this page to enable or block outbound voice calls to specific countries for a specific account. Calls to countries not enabled here will be blocked. Navigate: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → enter username → Country Permissions tab.

nav_path: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → Country Permissions (scroll 3)
caption: Voice Geo Permissions — Country Permissions, scroll 3. Countries visible: Dominican Republic (North America — Can Override From Console=ON, enabled), Algeria (Africa — OFF), Ecuador (South America — OFF), Estonia (Europe — OFF). Shows how individual countries are configured — Dominican Republic has console override enabled meaning the customer can toggle it themselves. Most countries are disabled by default. To enable outbound voice calls to a country for an account, find the country and toggle it on, then Save Changes. Navigate: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → Country Permissions (scroll).

nav_path: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → Country Permissions (scroll 4)
caption: Voice Geo Permissions — Country Permissions, scroll 4. Countries visible: Saint Pierre and Miquelon (North America — Can Override=OFF), Pitcairn Islands (Oceania — OFF), Puerto Rico (North America — Can Override=ON, enabled — calls to Puerto Rico are allowed), Palestine (Asia — OFF). Puerto Rico showing Can Override=ON is notable — US-territory numbers may route through US carriers but still require explicit geo permission for direct dialing. Navigate: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → Country Permissions (scroll).

nav_path: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → Country Permissions (scroll 5)
caption: Voice Geo Permissions — Country Permissions, scroll 5. Countries visible: Ukraine (Europe — Can Override=OFF, disabled), Uganda (Africa — OFF), U.S. Minor Outlying Islands (Oceania — Can Override=ON, Custom Block=checked), United States (North America — Can Override=ON, Custom Block=checked). US has both Can Override From Console enabled AND Custom Block checked — this means US calling is platform-enabled but custom-blocked for this specific account. Custom Block overrides the toggle for this account. If a customer reports US calls are blocked despite US being in their account's voice geo permissions, check if Custom Block is checked. Navigate: Voice → Voice Geo Permissions → Country Permissions (scroll to bottom).

nav_path: Zentrunk → Trunks → Outbound
caption: Zentrunk Trunks page, Outbound tab in Ryuk. Search for outbound trunks by Trunk Domain or Auth ID. Results show: Trunk name, Domain, IP Group (click to see allowed IPs), Auth Group, Trunk Status (enabled/disabled), Trunk CPS. Example: CRSSTALK-Outbound trunk with domain 3061612387502241.zt.plivo.com. Used to verify Zentrunk outbound trunk configuration. Navigate: Zentrunk → Trunks → Outbound tab.

nav_path: Zentrunk → Trunks → Outbound → IP Group
caption: IP Group modal in Zentrunk Outbound Trunks. Click the IP Group link to see the IP addresses/CIDR ranges allowed to send SIP traffic on this trunk. Example: 3CX_SIL group shows 138.89.151.24/32. Used to verify or troubleshoot IP whitelisting for Zentrunk.

nav_path: Zentrunk → Trunks → Inbound
caption: Zentrunk Trunks page, Inbound tab in Ryuk. Search for inbound trunks by phone number or Auth ID. Results show: Trunk name, Numbers (DIDs assigned to trunk), Primary URI (SIP destination for inbound calls), Fallback URI, Trunk Status. Example: CRSSTALK-INBOUND trunk with numbers 17328101680 and 17324407338, Primary URI SIL-3CX. Navigate: Zentrunk → Trunks → Inbound tab.

nav_path: Zentrunk → Trunks → Inbound → URI Detail
caption: SIP URI detail modal in Zentrunk Inbound Trunks. Click the URI link to see the full SIP URI configuration. Example: SIL-3CX shows URI: 138.89.151.24:5061;transport=tls and Auth Enabled: False. Used to verify destination SIP URI and TLS/auth settings for inbound Zentrunk calls. Navigate: Zentrunk → Trunks → Inbound → click URI link.

nav_path: Zentrunk → Trunks → Inbound → URI Detail
caption: SIP URI detail modal in Zentrunk Inbound Trunks (additional view). Shows same URI configuration: URI, Auth Enabled status.

nav_path: Zentrunk → Fetch CDRs
caption: Zentrunk Fetch CDRs page in Ryuk. Two tabs: CDR (search) and Call Insights. Search form: Zentrunk Call UUID, Voice Call UUID, From Number, To Number, Date range, Hangup Cause, Direction (inbound/outbound), From/To Country, Carrier ID/Name, Domestic Call filter. Results table: Date, From, To, Account ID, Direction, To Country, Hangup Cause, Duration, Call Insights link (Generate button), STIR Verification, STIR Attestation. Navigate: Zentrunk → Fetch CDRs.

nav_path: Zentrunk → Fetch CDRs
caption: Zentrunk Fetch CDRs results page (second view/scroll). Shows the CDR list with all columns visible.

nav_path: Zentrunk → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail
caption: Zentrunk CDR Detail modal (scroll 1). Click a CDR row to see full details. Fields: Call UUID (Zentrunk), Call ID (Voice Call UUID linking to Voice CDR), To Number (with carrier/type), From Number, Initiation Time, Answer Time, End Time, Duration, Bill Duration, Call Direction, Destination Network Group, Origin Network Group, Hangup Cause, Call Rate, Total Amount (cost), Originator (customer/carrier), Hangup Code, Cause Description. Navigate: Zentrunk → Fetch CDRs → click a row.

nav_path: Zentrunk → Fetch CDRs → CDR Detail
caption: Zentrunk CDR Detail (scroll 2). nav_path: Messaging (left nav)
caption: Ryuk left navigation — Messaging section fully expanded. Sub-items: Outbound SMS/MMS Pricing, SMS/WA Cost Pricing, Dynamic Routing, Dynamic Routing Texter, Content Blocker, Outbound SMS Routing, SMS Configuration, Texter Test Schedule, Tollfree SMS/MMS Pricing, Template Management, Sender ID Registration, Sender ID Rate Limit, Error Code Mapping, Fetch MDRs, Debug Tool. Use this section for all SMS/MMS account investigations, sender ID issues, DLT template approvals, 10DLC compliance, and delivery failures.

nav_path: Account Management → Accounts → [account] → Account Settings → Messaging Actions
caption: Account Settings page — Messaging-specific action buttons. Key buttons visible: Disable Messages at Operator Level (blocks outbound SMS/MMS at Plivo infrastructure level, stronger than account-level disable), Enable SMS Cost Check (sets a daily spend threshold that blocks SMS when exceeded — rate limiter, not just alert), Edit Product Plan, Update Account Product Type, Update Subscription Plan (three billing/tier buttons for changing account plan), Verify Proof (verifies business registration or KYC documents submitted by customer), Set as Staff User (grants internal Plivo staff privileges), Enable Bulk Call (enables simultaneous outbound dialing to multiple numbers), Manage USD Bank Transfer (manages customer wire transfer banking details), Change Customer Type (changes account tier: Regular/Enterprise/Partner/Reseller), Schedule Conversion to Postpaid (schedules future billing switch from prepaid to postpaid), Port-out No Response Config (configures automatic rejection/approve behaviour when port-out request gets no response), Check Email Bounce Status (checks whether Plivo notification emails to the customer are bouncing). Navigate: Account Management → Accounts → [search customer] → Account Settings → scroll to action buttons.

nav_path: Messaging → Template Management
caption: Template Management page in Ryuk — initial state before search. Search fields: Account (Auth ID), DLT Template ID, Sender ID, Status dropdown, Category dropdown. Results table headers visible: DLT Template ID, Sender ID, Status, Category, Template, Created At, Actions. Used for India DLT (Distributed Ledger Technology) template compliance — all SMS sent to Indian numbers must use a pre-registered DLT template. Navigate: Messaging → Template Management.

nav_path: Messaging → Template Management → Category dropdown
caption: Template Management — Category filter dropdown showing all DLT template categories for Indian SMS. Options: Transactional (banking, financial, critical alerts — highest priority, no promotional content allowed), Promotional (marketing messages, require prior customer consent), Service Implicit (service updates where customer relationship is implied — utility, delivery notifications), Service Explicit (service messages where customer explicitly opted in). Use this filter to find templates of a specific category when investigating DLT rejection or delivery failure to Indian numbers.

nav_path: Messaging → Template Management → Status dropdown
caption: Template Management — Status filter dropdown showing DLT template approval statuses. Options: Approved (template cleared by TRAI regulator via DLT portal — SMS can be sent), Pending (submitted, awaiting TRAI approval — SMS blocked until approved), Rejected (TRAI rejected template — must resubmit with corrections), In Review (currently under TRAI review). When a customer reports SMS delivery failure to Indian numbers, check this page for their template status. Rejected or Pending status is the most common root cause for Indian SMS delivery failures. Navigate: Messaging → Template Management → Status filter.

nav_path: Messaging → Sender ID Registration
caption: Sender ID Registration page in Ryuk. Search by Account (Auth ID), Sender ID (alphanumeric name shown to recipient), Destination Country, Status. Results table: Sender ID, Account, Country, Status (Approved/Pending/Rejected/Blocked), Carrier Mapping, Created At, Actions. Used for investigating why a customer's alphanumeric sender ID is not working or not delivering in a specific country. Many countries require pre-registration of sender IDs with local carriers before SMS can be sent. Navigate: Messaging → Sender ID Registration.

nav_path: Messaging → Sender ID Registration → Carrier Mapping
caption: Sender ID Registration — Carrier Mapping view. Shows which carriers the sender ID has been submitted to or approved by for a given country. Columns: Carrier Name, Status (Approved/Pending/Rejected), Submitted At, Approved At. A sender ID may be approved with some carriers but not others in the same country — SMS will only deliver through approved carriers. If a customer reports inconsistent delivery (some recipients get it, others don't), check carrier mapping to see which carriers have approved the sender ID.

nav_path: Messaging → Sender ID Registration → History
caption: Sender ID Registration — History tab. Shows the full audit trail of status changes for a sender ID: creation, carrier submissions, approvals, rejections, and any manual support actions. Columns: Action, Status, Actor (support agent or system), Notes, Created At. Use this to understand why a sender ID was rejected or blocked, and what actions have already been taken. Check this before escalating a sender ID issue to avoid duplicate submissions.

nav_path: Messaging → Error Code Mapping
caption: Error Code Mapping page in Ryuk — list view. Maps Plivo's internal error codes to carrier-specific error codes and descriptions. Columns: Plivo Error Code, Carrier Error Code, Carrier Name, Description, Country, Created At. Used when a customer reports SMS delivery failure with a specific error code from Plivo's delivery webhook. Look up the Plivo error code here to find the corresponding carrier error and understand the exact failure reason (e.g., spam filter, number inactive, DLT violation). Navigate: Messaging → Error Code Mapping.

nav_path: Messaging → Error Code Mapping → Plivo Master List
caption: Error Code Mapping — Plivo Master Error Code list. Shows all standardised Plivo SMS error codes with their definitions: error code number, short name, full description of what caused the failure, and recommended action. Key codes visible: codes for carrier rejection, DLT violation, sender ID not registered, number not reachable, opt-out, spam filter triggered. Use this as reference when explaining error codes to customers or diagnosing why their SMS webhook shows a specific error_code field.

nav_path: Messaging → Fetch MDRs
caption: Fetch MDRs (Message Detail Records) page in Ryuk. Search fields: Account (Auth ID), From Number, To Number, Message UUID, Date Range (From/To), Status filter (queued/sent/delivered/undelivered/failed/received), Direction (inbound/outbound). Results show per-message records: Message UUID, From, To, Direction, Status, Error Code, Carrier, Submitted At, Delivered At, Price. Use Fetch MDRs to investigate specific delivery failures — search by Message UUID from customer's webhook payload, or by To number + date range to find a specific message. Check Status and Error Code columns for root cause. Navigate: Messaging → Fetch MDRs.

nav_path: Messaging → Outbound SMS Routing (Outgoing Carriers)
caption: Outgoing Carriers page in Ryuk — first scroll. Shows the SMS carrier routing configuration for accounts. Columns: Account, Carrier Name, Country Code, Message Type (SMS/MMS), Priority, Status (Active/Inactive), Created At. Used when a customer reports that SMS is routing through the wrong carrier, or when carrier-level routing changes are needed. Agents with carrier relations access can update carrier assignments or priorities here. Navigate: Messaging → Outbound SMS Routing.

nav_path: Messaging → Outbound SMS Routing (Outgoing Carriers) → scroll
caption: Outgoing Carriers — second scroll showing additional carrier routing entries and action buttons. Each row has Edit and Delete action buttons. Carrier entries cover different countries and message types (SMS/MMS). Multiple carriers can be configured per country with different priorities — the highest priority active carrier is used first. If primary carrier fails, system falls through to lower-priority carriers. Check this page when a customer reports SMS routing issues or unexpected carrier changes.

nav_path: Messaging → Powerpack (via account or Outbound SMS Routing)
caption: Powerpack page in Ryuk. Powerpack is a pool of phone numbers that auto-selects the optimal sending number for each message based on destination, carrier performance, and compliance. Shows: Powerpack UUID, Account, Name, Status (Active/Paused/Disabled), Number Pool Size, Sticky Sender (on/off — whether same sender number is used for messages to same recipient), Application, Created At, Actions. Used when a customer reports issues with Powerpack number selection, sticky sender not working, or Powerpack disabled. Navigate: Messaging → (search for Powerpack in Outbound SMS Routing or via account).

nav_path: Messaging → SMS Geo Permissions
caption: SMS Geo Permissions page in Ryuk — before account search. Search field: Account (Auth ID). Used to view and modify which countries a specific account is allowed to send SMS to. All countries are disabled by default for new accounts; each country must be explicitly enabled. This is the first place to check when a customer reports that SMS to a specific country is not going through — the country may simply not be enabled for their account. Navigate: Messaging → SMS Geo Permissions → enter Auth ID.

nav_path: Messaging → SMS Geo Permissions → [account loaded]
caption: SMS Geo Permissions — account loaded, showing full country list. Each row: Country Name, Country Code, Enabled (Yes/No toggle), Hard Disabled (locked at platform level — cannot be enabled by support without escalation), Last Updated. Most countries show Enabled=No and Hard Disabled=No by default (can be enabled by support). Some high-risk countries or countries without carrier coverage show Hard Disabled=Yes (cannot be enabled). To enable SMS to a country for an account, find the country row and toggle Enabled to Yes. Navigate: Messaging → SMS Geo Permissions → [enter Auth ID] → find country.

nav_path: Messaging → SMS Geo Permissions → filter United States
caption: SMS Geo Permissions — filtered to show United States. US row shows: Country=United States, Code=US, Enabled=Yes, Hard Disabled=No. For US SMS, geo permissions are typically already enabled (US is the primary market). If US SMS is failing for an account, the root cause is usually 10DLC campaign registration, A2P compliance, or carrier-level filtering — not geo permissions. Use this filter to quickly confirm US is enabled before ruling out geo permissions as the cause.

nav_path: Messaging → SMS Geo Permissions → filter India
caption: SMS Geo Permissions — filtered to show India. India row shows: Country=India, Code=IN, Enabled status, Hard Disabled=No. For India SMS, geo permissions must be enabled AND DLT template must be registered and approved. A customer can have geo permissions enabled but still fail if their DLT template is pending or rejected. When investigating Indian SMS delivery failure: (1) check geo permissions here, (2) check DLT template status in Template Management, (3) check sender ID registration if using alphanumeric sender.

nav_path: Messaging → SMS Geo Permissions → filter Canada
caption: SMS Geo Permissions — filtered to show Canada. Canada row shows: Country=Canada, Code=CA, Enabled status. For Canada SMS, 10DLC-equivalent compliance (Canadian long code registration) may be required for A2P messaging. If a customer reports SMS to Canada is blocked or undelivered, check: (1) geo permissions enabled here, (2) whether 10DLC/SHAFT compliance is needed for their use case, (3) MDR error codes via Fetch MDRs.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Profiles tab
caption: 10DLC & Tollfree Management — Profiles tab. The Profile is the first step in the 10DLC compliance pipeline: Profile → Brand → Campaign → Numbers. A Profile represents the company/entity registering to send A2P SMS. Search by Account (Auth ID) or Profile ID. Results show: Profile ID, Account, Company Name, Tax ID / EIN, Address, Status (Approved/Pending/Rejected), Created At. A rejected or missing Profile blocks all downstream Brand and Campaign creation. Navigate: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Profiles.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Profiles → results
caption: 10DLC Profiles — results table showing registered profiles. Columns: Profile ID (UUID), Account (Auth ID), Company Name, Tax ID (EIN), Company Address, Status (Approved/Pending/Rejected/Failed), Created At, Actions (View/Edit). Each customer account should have one Profile. If Status=Rejected, view the rejection reason in the Actions menu and advise the customer to correct their company information (correct legal name, valid EIN, matching address). A profile rejection blocks all 10DLC registration.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Brands tab
caption: 10DLC & Tollfree Management — Brands tab. A Brand represents the business entity registered with The Campaign Registry (TCR) — second step after Profile. Search by Account (Auth ID), Brand ID, or Brand Name. Results: Brand ID, Account, Brand Name, Profile, Brand Type (Standard/Low Volume/Sole Proprietor), Identity Status (Vetted/Unvetted), TCR Status (Registered/Failed/Pending), Created At. A Brand must be TCR-registered before Campaigns can be created. Sole Proprietor brands have a daily message limit of 75 messages. Navigate: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Brands.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Brands → scroll
caption: 10DLC Brands — scrolled view showing additional brand details and action buttons. Each brand row shows: Brand ID, EIN, vetting status, TCR registration status, and Actions (View, Edit, Resubmit to TCR). Brands with FAILED or SUSPENDED status cannot have new campaigns created. Use Resubmit when a brand was rejected due to missing or incorrect information. Identity Vetting (optional, paid process) upgrades a brand and may increase campaign throughput limits.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Campaigns tab
caption: 10DLC & Tollfree Management — Campaigns tab. A Campaign defines the use case for sending SMS (e.g., 2FA, Marketing, Customer Care) — third step after Brand. Search by Account (Auth ID), Campaign ID, or Use Case. Results: Campaign ID, Account, Brand, Use Case (2FA/Marketing/Customer Care/etc.), Status (Active/Failed/Expired/Pending Review), CSP Status, MNO Status (per-carrier approval), Created At. Numbers must be linked to an Active campaign before A2P SMS can be sent. Navigate: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Campaigns.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Campaigns → failure reasons
caption: 10DLC Campaigns — Failure Reasons modal or column showing why a campaign was rejected by TCR or carrier MNOs. Common failure reasons visible: INVALID_USECASE (use case doesn't match message content described), CONTENT_VIOLATION (sample messages contain prohibited content — e.g. SHAFT: Sex, Hate, Alcohol, Firearms, Tobacco), MISSING_EMBEDDED_LINK (campaign claims to include URLs but sample messages don't show them), MISSING_OPT_IN_MESSAGE (opt-in language not included), SUBSCRIBER_OPT_IN (opt-in process not clearly described). Each failure reason maps to a specific fix the customer must make before resubmitting the campaign. Navigate: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Campaigns → [campaign row] → view failure reasons.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Campaigns → scroll
caption: 10DLC Campaigns — scrolled view showing MNO (Mobile Network Operator) per-carrier status columns. Each major US carrier (AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon, US Cellular) has its own approval status: Approved, Rejected, Pending. A campaign can be Active overall but rejected by one specific carrier — SMS to recipients on that carrier will fail. If a customer reports that SMS delivers to some recipients but not others, check the per-MNO status here. An AT&T or T-Mobile rejection affects a large portion of US recipients.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Numbers tab
caption: 10DLC & Tollfree Management — Numbers tab. Shows which phone numbers are linked to which campaigns. A number must be linked to an Active campaign before it can send A2P SMS. Search by Account, Phone Number, or Campaign ID. Results: Phone Number, Account, Campaign ID, Campaign Status, Linked At, Actions. If a customer reports that a specific number is not delivering SMS, check here to confirm the number is linked to an active campaign. If no campaign link exists, the number cannot send A2P traffic — customer must link it to an appropriate campaign. Navigate: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Numbers.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Tollfree Verifications tab
caption: 10DLC & Tollfree Management — Tollfree Verifications tab. Tollfree numbers (8XX numbers) require separate verification before A2P SMS can be sent at volume. Search by Account (Auth ID) or Tollfree Number. Results: Verification ID, Account, Tollfree Number, Use Case, Status (Approved/Pending/Rejected/Unverified), Submitted At. An unverified tollfree number has a daily sending limit of 500 messages. Approved verification lifts this limit. Common rejection reason: sample messages don't match the stated use case. Navigate: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Tollfree Verifications.

nav_path: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Tollfree Numbers tab
caption: 10DLC & Tollfree Management — Tollfree Numbers tab. Lists all tollfree numbers (800/833/844/855/866/877/888) associated with accounts, their verification status, and linked verification record. Columns: Phone Number, Account, Verification ID, Verification Status, Linked Campaign (if any), Created At. Use this tab to find a customer's tollfree number and confirm whether it has an approved verification. If Verification Status=Unverified or no verification linked, the number is capped at 500 messages/day. Navigate: Messaging → 10DLC & Tollfree Management → Tollfree Numbers.
